sections.html:
Kennett's courthouse square holds the two elected offices that shape a Dunklin County tax bill. One sets the value and the other sends the bill and cashes the check. Both are at 100 Kennett Court Square, Kennett, MO 63857.

Judy Thompson is Collector-Treasurer, in Room 203, phone 573-888-2180, mailing address PO Box 445. Rena Ingram is the assessor, reachable at 573-888-1409 or 573-888-4771. The recorder of deeds is Angela Casey, 573-888-3468.

Money the collector takes in is passed along to every district that levies on the parcel: ambulance, health center, library, schools, state, townships, the road and bridge fund and the sheltered workshop. A city levy is billed separately by the city. Never combine it with a county check.

Dunklin County fills part of Missouri's far southeastern Bootheel, with Kennett as seat and largest town. The population estimate is 26,855, a drop of 5.1 percent from 28,292 in April 2020. Of 13,520 housing units, 62.3 percent are owner-occupied. The median owned home is worth $97,600, against median rent of $648.

Values this low keep the yearly tax to a few hundred dollars, but a neglected year can still eat into what a seller walks away with. Houses inside Kennett, Malden, Senath or Clarkton also owe the town, so ask both offices what is open.

sections.h2: How a house gets its taxable value
sections.html:
The assessor lists every taxable parcel annually. New values are set as of January 1 of odd-numbered years and stay in place through the next even year unless the property was improved. Under RSMo 137.115 a house is counted at 19 percent of its true value, cropland at 12 and commercial buildings at 32, and each district's levy runs against that smaller figure.

A residential jump of more than 15 percent, unless it comes from new building, requires an in-person inspection first. Owners can request a look inside and have at least 30 days to make that request. A drive-by does not satisfy the rule.

If you switch a property from farm to residential use, apply to the assessor to have it reclassified. Personal property filings can be made online through the assessor's page.

The notice comes first. RSMo 137.180 requires the assessor to mail any increase to the record owner's last known address, and in a reassessment year that mailing is due by June 15. If the figure looks wrong, phone the assessor with recent sale prices for similar houses.

The formal venue is the county Board of Equalization (RSMo 138.060), which does not start from a presumption that the assessor is right. The assessor must carry the proof only when a value climbed 15 percent or more without new construction. The filing cutoff is the second Monday in July, which will be July 12 in 2027. The Dunklin County Clerk can tell you where the form goes.

A loss at the Board can go to the State Tax Commission, with a complaint due September 30 or 30 days after the Board's final action, whichever falls later. Property titled to a company, trust or estate must go through an attorney. Send the tax bill or the Board's decision letter with the complaint and save the rest of your evidence until the Commission asks.

sections.h2: Due dates, penalties and collector rules
sections.html:
December 31 is the due date. RSMo 139.100 counts a mailed payment as made on its postmark date, so an envelope stamped that day is timely. Starting January 1 the collector adds the penalty fixed by RSMo 140.100: 18 percent of the year's delinquency, with a monthly cap of 2 percent for land redeemed before the sale.

Know these counter rules before driving to Kennett:

  • Bring the stub. Without it the check is sent back, and a walk-in payer is charged to print a duplicate.
  • Only full payment is taken. Part-cash, part-check combinations are turned away too.
  • Accepted tender: cash, debit or credit cards, bank checks, money orders, and personal checks that carry an address, phone number and driver license number.
  • Delinquent years go first. Current-year tax will not be accepted until older balances are paid.
  • Nothing is quoted over the phone. Come to Room 203, fax a request (a $3 fee applies per parcel) or write.

You can pay a disputed bill under protest. Pay all of it before it goes delinquent, put the reasons and your claimed value in writing, and sue the collector inside 90 days as RSMo 139.031 provides. Tax paid by mistake can be refunded if you claim it within three years.

Each year on the fourth Monday of August, RSMo 140.150 has the collector offer land with taxes unpaid for two years. Parcels that draw no buyer after a third offering can be purchased with the deed issued on the spot.

Up to the day of the sale you can wipe out the debt by paying the tax, penalty, interest and costs. Notice goes out by ordinary mail, with a certified second letter when the assessed value tops $1,000. If the mail never reaches you, the debt still stands.

With old years open on your house, mark that August Monday as the last safe day. Pay ahead of it and the house stays out of the offering.

All three open at 8:30 a.m. and close at 4:30 p.m., so one trip to the square can cover the bill, the value and the deed.

Request an up-to-date statement in Room 203 before listing. Any earlier year gets paid ahead of this one. Give your closing agent the parcel number and the collector's phone so the payoff matches what the office has on file. Your sales contract, not the county, decides how this year's bill is divided with the buyer.

On the deed side, the recorder's fees changed on August 27, 2026. A one-page document is $26, and each extra page up to 20 pages adds $3. Plats and surveys are priced separately. Missouri counties accept electronic filing through a shared portal, so ask Room 204 if filing online suits your closing.

Liens, tenants or a failing roof can stall a conventional sale of a Kennett-area house. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal, and the tax payoff is taken from your proceeds at the closing table.

faqs.q: Who bills Dunklin County property tax?
faqs.a: Judy Thompson's office, the Collector-Treasurer, mails it. The assessor's job ends at the value, and any city tax arrives on a separate bill.

faqs.q: When are Dunklin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 31. An envelope postmarked that day is on time, and the 18 percent penalty begins January 1.

faqs.q: Can I pay part of my Dunklin County bill?
faqs.a: No, the counter takes only the whole amount and refuses mixed cash and check. Back years have to be settled before this year's tax is accepted.

faqs.q: When are delinquent Dunklin County houses sold?
faqs.a: Land two years behind is offered on the fourth Monday of August. Paying the tax, penalty and costs before that day pulls it from the list.

faqs.q: How do I dispute my Dunklin County home value?
faqs.a: Phone the assessor, then file with the Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. The State Tax Commission hears any further appeal.
